Hi Samantha / John,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great discussion. As promised, I'd like to start the capacity sizing conversation for a private VPC deployment so we can pin recommendations for throughput and redundancy. 

High-level asks to help our SRE/SE team size the private GPU pool:
- Typical steady-state request rate (requests/sec) and typical peak bursts (duration + rps)
- Expected distribution by model: lightweight (<=8B) vs heavy (>=70B) and % split
- Average input + generation tokens per request and any long-tail large-context use cases
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) you want for interactive features vs async batch jobs
- KV cache hit rate expectations and whether prefix sharing is possible across sessions
- Any constraints on cross-AZ traffic, private peering, or egress rules we should be aware of

If you can paste those numbers into a quick reply we will run a sizing matrix and return an initial recommendation + warmup/runbook. Next step from our side would be a 30-min architecture sync with Laura and Dev to walk the assumptions.

Thanks,
--

Hi Karthik,

Thanks — happy to share initial numbers so you can put together something concrete. Our traffic today (approx):
- Steady-state: 120 rps (mix of health-checking/agent traffic and user-facing requests)
- Peak: up to ~600 rps for short bursts (8-15 minutes) twice a day (09:00-09:20 and 18:00-18:15 local)
- Model mix: 70% small models (~6–8B) for short replies, 30% large models (~40–70B) used for rich summarization and clinical inference
- Tokens: median 80 tokens in, ~150 tokens generated for interactive flows; heavy batch jobs up to 2,000 tokens (rare, nightly)
- Latency targets: interactive p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms (hard target for clinician UX). For batch jobs we accept higher latency.
- KV cache: we expect moderate prefix reuse across sessions; approximate hit-rate 55–65% once warmed
- Networking: VPC peering to our staging and prod VPCs; prefer AZ-local routing and no outbound internet egress from private pool.

Two other asks: can you size for 2-az redundancy (failover within region) and provide recommendations on warm-up/cold-cache strategies? Also loop in procurement — I'll copy them if we start to talk pricing/commits.

Samantha Dunn
Dir. of Engineering, Greenfield Health

Hi Samantha — thanks for the details. Based on these inputs we ran a quick sizing exercise and attached a working capacity matrix (gfh-capacity-matrix-v1.xlsx) plus a short warmup playbook. Summary highlights and assumptions below — please review and flag anything that doesn't match your traffic profile.

Key sizing assumptions
- Small model (8B): avg generation ~150 tokens -> ~0.9 tokens/ms on A100/80GB with Redwood runtime optimizations (assumption: quantized kernels).
- Large model (40–70B): avg generation ~700 tokens for heavy flows; use 2x memory-parallel shards, slower tokens/s.
- Average request CPU/IO overhead: 6–10ms per request for routing/security in VPC environment.
- Batching: we plan for continuous batching window of 25–40ms for interactive requests (keeps p95 healthy).

Recommendation (initial, region-us, 2-AZ resilient):
- Minimum active pool: 6x A100-80GB GPUs sized for steady-state 120 rps with a target 20% headroom (handles token throughput for mixed model mix).
- Scaleable burst capacity: additional 6 GPUs in warm standby that can be brought online within 60–90s; autoscale policy tied to queue depth and p95 latency crossing 220ms for >45s.
- Cold-start mitigation: pre-warm KV caches via synthetic replay jobs (nightly + 15-min pre-burst warmers) and maintain a small pool of pinned embeddings workers to avoid embedding cold-starts.
- Cache strategy: shard prefix caches per AZ, with periodic cross-AZ consistency syncs to limit inter-AZ egress; expected warmed hit-rate to reach 65% in 20–40 minutes after warmers run.

Failure / redundancy notes
- 2-AZ failover is feasible with cross-AZ replication for state-bearing services. For model-serving we recommend asymmetric capacity in each AZ (e.g., 6 active / 3 active) to limit cross-AZ requests during failover and accept brief latency increase while autoscaler spins up extra nodes.

Next steps
- I've uploaded the matrix and a warmup playbook to the shared Drive (link in the Drive folder).
- If this looks good, propose a 30-min architecture review to align SLA/burst policy and to confirm private peering config.

Attachments: gfh-capacity-matrix-v1.xlsx, warmup-playbook.md

Best,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
